01The record

What the work was for, and what changed

Two operating contexts, one method: keep each system with its owner, then join deliberately. Choose a context.

FAS Office for Faculty Affairs

Primary technical advisor to department chairs, preparing the data, reporting and meeting materials used by FAS deans, visiting committees and the Office of the Governing Boards.

I piloted the FAS DataHub (Oracle BI / HART) — a team effort that used my faculty-affairs reports as its blueprint. It joined seven sources inside a $1.8 billion operating environment with more than twenty years of longitudinal data.

Reusable dashboards replaced the request queue, so the same questions stopped arriving as one-off asks.

      UAMS · Phillips Academy

      The discipline was layered records: a constituent profile first, giving records on that constituent, and campaign finance counted from the giving records — not from a parallel spreadsheet.

      At UAMS I hired, supervised and reviewed the donor-records staff who kept those layers clean. At Phillips Academy the same method supported a comprehensive campaign and General Ledger bridge reconciliations with the Comptroller’s office.
